messages.author: a73b025ad2f2853f
messages.subject: Normalization:  Controls & Treated
parts:
Hi,
  For Normalization,  I perform it on all my samples control and treated in a same df ( which make most sense to me). I think MSstas normalize by equalizeMedian handle having controls and treated together without overestimating controls, is that correct?
I have been told to perform normalization for controls separately from treated to do not overestimate controls (background)??? 

I use:
summarized_processed_data_G4 <- MSstats::dataProcess(
  raw = input_data,          # Input preprocessed data
  logTrans = 2,
  normalization = "equalizeMedians",
  nameStandards = NULL,
  featureSubset = "all",
  remove_uninformative_feature_outlier = FALSE,
  min_feature_count = 2,
  n_top_feature = 3,
  summaryMethod = "TMP",
  equalFeatureVar = TRUE,
  censoredInt = "NA",
  MBimpute = TRUE,
  remove50missing = FALSE,
  fix_missing = NULL,
  maxQuantileforCensored = 0.999,
  use_log_file = TRUE,
  append = FALSE,
  verbose = TRUE,
  log_file_path = NULL,
  numberOfCores = 1
)

So according to you, what is the correct way to use :
MSstats::dataProcess
  normalization = "equalizeMedians" 

All samples controls & treated normalized together or each category separately ? 

Many thanks for your time and support,
Julie

messages.author: 13904eb0f06097b0
messages.subject: Re: Normalization: Controls & Treated
parts:
Hi Julie,

MSstats will normalize all runs together, both control and treated.

The key assumption here is that the majority of proteins are not changing across conditions (i.e., the majority of proteins are not differentially abundant between control and treated). This is likely a reasonable assumption in discovery experiments. In targeted experiments this may not be the case. Either way you can turn normalization off by setting `normalization = FALSE`

Devon
